req.title: PUT /players/{id} requires body
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when PUT /players/{playerId} is called without a request body.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-038 requires that PUT /players/{playerId} returns HTTP 422 when called without a request body. The actual endpoint in the source is PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}. Three tests are designed: (1) a negative test confirming 422 when no body is sent, (2) a positive test confirming 204 when a valid body is sent (proving the 422 is body-absence-specific, not a blanket error), and (3) a boundary test confirming that an empty JSON object {} (body present but missing required fields) also yields 422, distinguishing 'no body' from 'empty body'. All tests use exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator and constant mutations.

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_put_player_no_body_returns_422():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.put('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert response.status_code == 422

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_put_player_valid_body_returns_204():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Anjali",
        "lastName": "Banerjee",
        "squadNumber": 1,
        "position": "Defensive Midfield"
    }
    response = client.put('/players/squadnumber/1', json=payload)
    assert response.status_code == 204

test_put_player_valid_body_returns_204()

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_put_player_no_body_response_detail_structure():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.put('/players/squadnumber/2')
    assert response.status_code == 422
    body = response.json()
    assert 'detail' in body
    assert isinstance(body['detail'], list)
    assert len(body['detail']) >= 1

test_put_player_no_body_response_detail_structure()
